_note: The provenance of every captured artifact under tools/gates/fixtures. Written by hand, read by tools/gates/probes/readers.mjs (and by its `the captured fixtures are present` self-check in probes/_harness.mjs). Every entry says the exact command that produced the file and whether the bytes are VERBATIM output (real: true) or a named edit of real output (real: false, with `derivedFrom` and `edit`). A fixture nobody can re-capture is a fixture nobody can trust, so re-capture is the cure for a stale one — never a hand edit. No seconds figure is promised anywhere here; the `time`/`start_time` fields inside an artifact are that artifact's own content.

runnerMigration._note: The jest/* artifacts REPLACE the vitest/* set captured on 2026-11-01. They were re-captured rather than kept, because eighteen reader probes would otherwise assert a format this repository's runner no longer produces — the trap probes/_harness.mjs calls probing an imagined format. jest.config.mjs reproduces the file-path `classname` on purpose (classNameTemplate '{filepath}', titleTemplate '{classname} > {title}'), so the GREEN shape is unchanged; four MEASURED differences remain and each is written on the entry it belongs to.
measuredDifferences: a `<failure>` written by jest-junit 17.0.0 carries NO `message` and NO `type` attribute — both live in the element BODY, whose first line is `<Type>: <message>` (see jest/all-failed.junit.xml)

a suite that failed to RUN produces no `<testsuite>` and no `<testcase>` at all, so the XML of a collection failure is shaped exactly like an empty run (see jest/collection-failure.junit.xml against jest/empty-run.junit.xml)
`it.todo` is a `<testcase>` with NO `<skipped/>` child, and the `tests`/`skipped` counters exclude it, while the JSON channel counts it in numTodoTests (see jest/skipped-only.*)

the runner's own collection, `jest --listTests --json`, is an array of absolute FILE paths — not one record per case, so it corroborates which project collects a file and says nothing about case names (see jest/list-core.json)

commandShape._note: Every `command` below is shorthand for this shape, run from the repository root. The JUnit path is NOT a flag: jest-junit is declared as a reporter in jest.config.mjs with no `outputFile` and takes its path from the ENVIRONMENT, so half of the artifact contract travels in env and `run.json` records it as `envExtra`.
commandShape.measured: without NODE_OPTIONS every test file dies with `Cannot use import statement outside a module`, which reads like a broken source and is not one. With JEST_JUNIT_OUTPUT_FILE unset, jest-junit writes ./junit.xml into the cwd — observed in this repository's root during the capture session, which is exactly why no caller may leave the path to a default.

sources._note: sha256 of the committed test sources a fixture was captured FROM. A probe that compares a stored artifact against a live source reads these first and SKIPS with `re-capture` when they disagree — a stale fixture must never read as a defect in the reader.

captureFixtures._note: The four `packages/core/test/__cap/*.test.ts` files the jest/* artifacts were captured FROM. They are planted for the capture and removed in the same session, so they are not committed and their names survive only inside the artifacts and here. Each is listed with the situation it produces, so the capture can be repeated exactly.
captureFixtures.packages/core/test/__cap/one.test.ts: one passing case: `describe('the captured green case') > it('names the package')` asserting CORE_PACKAGE === '@cheq/core' against ../../src/index.ts
captureFixtures.packages/core/test/__cap/failed.test.ts: three failing cases in one describe('the three captured red signatures'): an honest `expect(...).toBe('@cheq/nope')`, a call of `core.completeTask()` which is not exported, and a bare `absentFn()` nobody wrote
captureFixtures.packages/core/test/__cap/skipped.test.ts: one `it.skip('is switched off')` and one `it.todo('is not written yet')` in describe('the captured skipped cases')
captureFixtures.packages/core/test/__cap/collect.test.ts: an import of ../../src/scheduling/schedule.ts, which does not exist, so the suite never runs

jest/core-skeleton.junit.xml.note: The committed tree's own core run: 17 cases over 2 files, all green, exit 0. `classname` is the REPO-relative file path and `name` is `<describe> > <test>` — the shape jest.config.mjs's reporter templates reproduce. Carries the case `hashes "abc"` as `"abc"`, which is the XML side of the escaping measurement. `--testPathPatterns 'test/skeleton/'` scopes the run to the COMMITTED files: a bare `--selectProjects core` also collects whatever is planted under packages/core/test at capture time.

jest/core-skeleton.json.note: numTotalTests 17, numPassedTests 17. Every `testResults[].name` is an ABSOLUTE path (measured), which is why jsonCaseStatus matches a file by suffix.

jest/list-core.json.edit: the absolute paths were made repo-relative; nothing else
jest/list-core.json.note: The runner's own collection. MEASURED and different from the previous runner: this is an array of test FILES, not one record per case, so it is the second answer to "which project collects this file" and no answer at all about case names. The prose line `Running one project: core` goes to STDERR, so stdout is pure JSON. The live absolute form is probed live, where it is honest.

jest/one-passed.junit.xml.note: One case, passed, exit 0. The ordinary green shape, and the baseline the mismatch pair is derived from.

jest/all-failed.junit.xml.note: The three red signatures in ONE artifact, exit 1 — AND the first measured difference from the previous runner: jest-junit writes `<failure>` with NO `message` and NO `type` ATTRIBUTE. The type and message are the first line of the element BODY: `Error: expect(received).toBe(expected) …`, `TypeError: core.completeTask is not a function`, `ReferenceError: absentFn is not defined`, each followed by the stack. parseJUnit therefore reads type='' and message='' for all three, and redReason answers `unknown` — recorded here as the artifact's own shape, not as a verdict about the reader.

jest/all-failed.json.note: numTotalTests 3, numFailedTests 3. Here the type and message DO survive, inside assertionResults[].failureMessages[0].

jest/skipped-only.junit.xml.note: MEASURED: `it.skip` becomes `<testcase><skipped/></testcase>`, and `it.todo` becomes a `<testcase>` with an EMPTY body — no `<skipped/>` child. The counters agree with that and not with the file: `<testsuites tests="1">`, `<testsuite tests="1" skipped="1">`, two `<testcase>` elements. The run exits 0.

jest/skipped-only.json.note: numTotalTests 2, numPendingTests 1 (the .skip), numTodoTests 1 (the .todo) — the one channel that tells them apart, and the one that counts the .todo at all. `testResults[0].status` is "focused"; file status is not a verdict.

jest/collection-failure.junit.xml.note: MEASURED signature, and the second difference from the previous runner: a suite that failed to RUN produces NO `<testsuite>` and NO `<testcase>`. The whole artifact is `<testsuites name="jest tests" tests="0" failures="0" errors="0">` — shaped exactly like jest/empty-run.junit.xml, while the run exits 1. There is no synthetic testcase whose classname/name pair could be compared, so the suffix form isCollectionFailure() looks for cannot occur in a jest artifact at all.

jest/collection-failure.json.note: The ONLY channel that sees the failure: numRuntimeErrorTestSuites 1, numFailedTestSuites 1, numTotalTests 0, success false, and testResults[0] with status "failed", assertionResults [] and the resolver's message. So the file that never loaded is nameable from the JSON and from nowhere else.

jest/empty-run.junit.xml.note: MEASURED: tests="0", a well-formed report, and the run EXITS 0. This is the silent green that `tests="0" ⇒ CANNOT VERIFY` exists for. --passWithNoTests is what makes the exit 0; it exists in Jest 30.5.2 and is the flag tools/gates/run.mjs refuses a caller for passing, and never passes itself — without it this same filter exits 1.

jest/foreign-file.junit.xml.command: jest --selectProjects api --ci --runInBand --json --outputFile=<abs>  (the api project whole, no filter)
jest/foreign-file.junit.xml.note: A real run of ANOTHER project: every classname is under apps/api. Asked about a core file, a reader must answer CANNOT VERIFY rather than reading somebody else's green.

jest/counter-mismatch.junit.xml.note: The XML half of the disagreement pair: tests="1".

jest/counter-mismatch.json.edit: numTotalTests and numPassedTests raised from 1 to 2
jest/counter-mismatch.json.note: No run has been observed producing two channels that disagree about a well-formed run (TD-0005), so this fixture is the ONLY way to exercise crossCheck's refusal on a counter. The ONE real disagreement this toolchain does produce — a .todo counted by the JSON and not by the XML — is in jest/skipped-only.* and needs no derivation.

oxlint/zero-files.raw.json.note: MEASURED and not what the design assumed: stdout carries the PROSE line `No files found to lint. Please check your paths and ignore patterns.` BEFORE the JSON, and oxlint exits 1. Since the lint lane's artifact IS oxlint's stdout, the artifact of a zero-file run is not valid JSON at all.

oxlint/zero-files.derived.json.note: What the reader's `number_of_files === 0` branch was written against. It is reachable only when a caller strips the prose line, which nothing does today — the raw fixture is the honest one, and this one exists so that branch is still exercised.
